To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

tobacco chewers are exposed to tobacco specific and mutagenic agents in the gastric fluid and that the mutagenicity of gastric fluid is due to nitrosation of tobacco specific agents and the generation of reactive oxygen species.
tobacco chewers have a high risk of developing cancer of the mouth, throat, and stomach because of the mutagenic chemicals in their saliva.
the gastric fluid of tobacco chewers is directly mutagenic to Salmonella typhymurium strains TA102, TA98 and TA100 and that reactive oxygen species may play an important role in the mutagenicity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an assay for detecting mutagenic exposure in tobacco chewers and non-users.
the mutagenic potential of gastric fluid from individuals who use tobacco in various ways.
the identification of the mutagenic and carcinogenic agents in gastric juice from tobacco chewers, and the role of these agents in gastric cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of tobacco with lime is a major risk factor for the induction of cancers of the oral cavity, pharynx and oesophagus.

tobacco chewing is an important risk factor for the development of cancer in the oral cavity and upper alimentary canal and that the mutagenic activity of the gastric juice from tobacco chewers may contribute to the development of cancer.

nitrosamines, ROS and nitrites are the main factors responsible for mutagenic activity of tobacco chewers' gastric fluid and the mutagenic activity may be attributed to the presence of these compounds.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mutagenicity of gastric fluid samples from chewers was directly mutagenic to TA98, TA102 and TA100, but required prior nitrosation in the presence of nitrite and S9 to TA98 and TA100.
tobacco chewing with lime is mutagenic in gastric fluid.
tobacco chewing is associated with a high incidence of gastric cancer and the mutagenic activity of tobacco chewers' gastric fluid may be due to the presence of nitrite and cotinne.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mutagenic activity of tobacco with lime chewers' gastric fluid is due to the presence of reactive oxygen species and that these species are responsible for the oxidative damage to DNA.
the use of tobacco in any form, whether it be chewing or smoking, is a major risk factor for cancer.
nitrosated tobacco chewed lime juice is a major source of mutagens in the gastric fluid.
